questions.q: What happens when you create a shortcut to another lakehouse's table?
options: A new, separate Delta table is created with duplicated data
The table appears in the second lakehouse too, marked with a link icon — the same underlying Delta files, read through a different front door
The original table is moved out of the first lakehouse entirely
The data is physically copied into the second lakehouse's own storage
questions.explain: This is Lesson 3's preview made concrete — nothing physically duplicated.

questions.q: What's the difference between an internal and an external shortcut?
options: External shortcuts only work within the same workspace
Internal points to another OneLake location (another lakehouse/workspace); external points to data outside Fabric entirely, like ADLS Gen2 or S3
There's no real difference between the two types
Internal shortcuts copy data; external shortcuts never copy data
questions.explain: External shortcuts read data in place, with nothing physically moved into Fabric's own storage.

questions.q: Do PySpark methods behave differently when reading from a shortcut-backed table versus the original?
options: No — every method works identically; the query engine simply resolves to wherever the real bytes live, with no special handling
Yes, shortcuts require a completely separate API
Yes, only read operations work on shortcuts, never filters or aggregations
Shortcuts cannot be queried with PySpark at all, only SQL
questions.explain: The transaction log and Foundations' Chapter 4 methods both apply unchanged.

questions.q: How does a Fabric shortcut compare to Databricks & Delta Lake's external table concept?
options: It's doing almost the same job — a reference to data whose actual bytes and lifecycle live elsewhere — just scoped to OneLake's reach instead of Unity Catalog's metastore
A shortcut is identical to a managed table, not an external one
They are completely unrelated concepts with no real similarity
External tables don't exist in either platform
questions.explain: Both reference data managed elsewhere, with the catalog/lake only tracking metadata, not the file lifecycle.

questions.q: What kind of data would an external shortcut typically point to?
options: An existing ADLS Gen2 container, Amazon S3 bucket, or similar storage outside Fabric
External shortcuts cannot point to any real storage location
Only data stored in a Fabric Warehouse, never a Lakehouse
Only data already stored inside another Fabric lakehouse
questions.explain: This connects directly to Foundations' entire Chapter 1, which covered ADLS Gen2 as real cloud storage.
